key_insight: PING embeds advection–diffusion physics in a graph neural network to forecast transport processes on irregular sensor networks and support solar power forecasting.
engineering_relevance: Better cloud-motion forecasts can improve intra-day photovoltaic power predictions and help integrate PV generation into the grid.
method: Represent transported particle concentrations as signals on a graph.
Use a discretized advection–diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the training loss.
Couple PING with PV forecasting models using ground-based sensor data and satellite cloud information.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on par with state-of-the-art models on synthetic and real transport datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index data, plus improved intra-day PV forecasting.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify PV forecasting gains, and a soft physics constraint does not guarantee physically consistent predictions.
paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
